fish.name: Bristlemouth
fish.flavor: The most numerous fish in the whole ocean, and it still gets nervous at parties. Catch one and a quadrillion siblings won't even notice.

fish.name: Tin Lanternfish
fish.flavor: Its photophores flicker like a cheap lamp with a loose wire. The locals read by them anyway, out of politeness.

fish.name: Pale Eelpout
fish.flavor: Pale, patient, and mildly damp in spirit. The trench's answer to a quiet neighbor who waves from the porch but never comes over.

fish.name: Trench Grenadier
fish.flavor: Named for its tapered tail, not its temper. Has never once exploded, despite persistent dockside rumors.

fish.name: Snubnose Snailfish
fish.flavor: Soft as a thumb pressed into dough, and utterly serene about it. Thrives under pressure, which is more than most of us can say.

fish.name: Sooty Hatchetfish
fish.flavor: Thin as a coin and twice as shifty. Its belly-lights erase its silhouette from below — the trench's oldest magic trick, still killing at parties.

fish.name: Dusky Cusk
fish.flavor: It has been slowly circling the same rock since before you were born, and it is very pleased with the rock. Ambition is a shallow-water disease.

fish.name: Pocket Angler
fish.flavor: An anglerfish the size of a plum, with a lure no brighter than a struck match. Everyone starts somewhere.

fish.name: Bashful Blobfish
fish.flavor: Perfectly handsome at depth, tragically misunderstood at the surface. Kindly admire it quickly and put it back before it gets embarrassed.

fish.name: Coalgill Slickhead
fish.flavor: Smooth-headed and unbothered, as if it combed its entire body back with pomade. Smells faintly of cold stone and good decisions.

fish.name: Pitch Darter
fish.flavor: Darts through the black like a rumor through a small town. Nobody has ever seen one sit still, including other Pitch Darters.

fish.name: Vesper Smelt
fish.flavor: Rises in great silver congregations at what the trench insists is evening. Down here, evening is a matter of faith.

fish.name: Velvet Whalefish
fish.flavor: Dressed in the deepest red money can't buy — a color no light reaches down here, so it's effectively invisible and extremely fancy about it.

fish.name: Fangtooth
fish.flavor: Owns the biggest teeth of any fish its size, with special sockets in its skull just so it can close its mouth. Nature's apology, delivered slightly too late.

fish.name: Umbrella Gulper
fish.flavor: Mostly mouth, then some more mouth, then a whip of a tail with a little light on the end. Attempts meals it has no business attempting, like an optimist at a buffet.

fish.name: Glasshead Barreleye
fish.flavor: Its transparent head shows two green eyes staring straight up, waiting. For what? It won't say. Up, though.

fish.name: Stiltwater Tripodfish
fish.flavor: Stands on three long fins for days, facing the current like it's waiting for a bus that comes twice a year. It always catches the bus.

fish.name: Needlelight Viperfish
fish.flavor: Its fangs are too long for its own mouth and its light too pretty for its face. The trench forgives both, because dinner needs catching.

fish.name: Greedy Swallower
fish.flavor: Once ate a fish four times its own size, then had a long, quiet think about its choices. It reached no conclusions and would do it again.

fish.name: Longnose Chimaera
fish.flavor: Older than sharks and quieter than churches. It reads the mud with its snout the way grandmothers read tea leaves, and it is just as smug about the results.

fish.name: Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: The widows on the coast say each one carries a candle lit for someone the sea kept. Release it gently, and say the name you're thinking of.

fish.name: Bellringer Eel
fish.flavor: Its jaws clack in the dark like a chapel bell at odd hours. Old trawlermen tip their caps and don't ask who the bell is for.

fish.name: Hushfish
fish.flavor: Swims so quietly the water forgets it was ever there. You don't hear a Hushfish bite — you just notice the silence has gotten heavier.

fish.name: Coffinfish
fish.flavor: Holds its breath for minutes at a time just to keep perfectly still — the trench's undefeated champion of hide-and-seek. Yes, that's its real name. No, it isn't sorry.

fish.name: Mirrorbelly Spook
fish.flavor: Its mirrored eyes gather light that fell into the trench centuries ago. Look closely and you might catch the glint of somebody's old summer.

fish.name: The Lamplighter
fish.flavor: Every dusk-that-isn't, something swims the length of the trench lighting the anglerfish lures one by one. The locals set their clocks by it, and the clocks keep perfect time.

fish.name: Old Sorrowjaw
fish.flavor: A fangtooth grown far past anything a fangtooth should be, with a face like an unpaid debt. Grandfathers swear it took their grandfathers' hooks, and the rusted hooks in its jaw agree.

fish.name: Grandmother Gloom
fish.flavor: A blobfish of tremendous age and gravity, wedged into her crevice like a warm loaf into a bread tin. The deep feels a little less frightening the moment you see her, which frightens some people worse.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Lantern
fish.flavor: When a ship goes down, a pale light comes, they say, and swims the drowned to wherever drowned folk go. Hook it and your line runs cold — reel gently, and it forgives you.

fish.name: Midnight Herself
fish.flavor: The trench isn't dark, the old song goes — it's Her shadow. When She passes overhead, every lure in the abyss goes out at once, out of respect.
